howItWorks.seoTitle: How Navilla Works — Your Private Sexual Health Companion
howItWorks.seoDescription: Learn how Navilla helps you track encounters, monitor your testing history, and stay informed with private tools, encrypted data, and anonymized exposure signals.
howItWorks.title: How It Works
howItWorks.subtitle: Everything Navilla does to help you take control of your sexual health — privately and on your terms.

overview.title: What is Navilla?
overview.body1: Navilla is a private sexual health companion. It gives you tools to track your encounters, monitor your testing history, manage partners, and see anonymized exposure signals from your network — all encrypted and under your control.
overview.body2: Some features are free and require no account (testing calculator, STI guides). Others — like the encounter journal, health log, and exposure network — require a free account so your data can be stored securely.

journal.title: Encounter Journal
journal.body1: A private, encrypted timeline where you log your sexual encounters. Only you can read it.
journal.item1: Log encounters with dates, partner aliases, and personal notes
journal.item2: Add custom fields like protection used, mood, or location
journal.item3: Switch between timeline view and calendar view to see your history from different angles
journal.item4: Use the calendar to quickly jump between months that have entries
journal.item5: All journal data is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it reaches the database

partners.title: Partner Tracking
partners.body1: When you use the same alias across multiple journal entries, Navilla can promote that alias to a named partner — giving you a dedicated view of your history with that person.
partners.item1: Each partner gets a detail page showing all encounters, notes, and a timeline
partners.item2: Add private notes to any partner (visible only to you)
partners.item3: See encounter counts and date ranges at a glance from the Partners tab
partners.body2: Partner data is encrypted the same way as journal entries. Navilla never shares partner information with anyone — not even the partner themselves.

healthLog.title: Health Log
healthLog.body1: Track every STI test visit in one place. Know exactly where you stand and what to test for next.
healthLog.item1: Log test visits with date, lab, and results per condition
healthLog.item2: Save your labs (clinic name, location) for quick reuse on future visits
healthLog.item3: See your full testing history organized by condition — with status, result values, and reference ranges
healthLog.item4: Track your coverage: how many of the 10 most common STIs you've been tested for this year
healthLog.item5: See days since your last test at a glance from the health log dashboard

network.title: Exposure Network
network.body1: When you connect with other Navilla users and they report a health status, you see anonymized exposure signals — never names or identifying details.
network.body2: Connections are stored as cryptographic hashes. Your network extends up to 5 degrees: if you're connected to Ana and Ana is connected to Luis, Luis is in your 2nd-degree network.
network.body3: If you have fewer than 3 connections, exposure data is hidden entirely. With only 1 or 2 connections, a signal could reveal a specific person's status. The 3-connection minimum protects everyone.
network.body4: Exposure signals are useful but have limitations:
network.item1: Exposure does not mean you are infected — it means someone in your extended network reported a condition
network.item2: Data is self-reported and may be delayed or incomplete
network.item3: The network only includes Navilla users — your real-world exposure may differ
network.item4: Exposure updates in delayed snapshots, not in real time, to prevent timing-based inference

freeTools.item2: STI guides — clear, plain-language guides on 10 common conditions covering symptoms, testing, and treatment

privacy.item2: Each user has a unique encryption key derived from a master secret

security.seoDescription: How Navilla encrypts and secures your data. Current encryption architecture and our roadmap toward end-to-end encryption.
security.title: Security
security.subtitle: How we protect your most sensitive data — and where we're headed.
security.encryptionTodayHeading: How your data is encrypted today
security.encryptionTodayBody1: Every sensitive field — partner names, encounter notes, health records, and personal identifiers — is encrypted at the application layer using AES-256-GCM before it reaches the database. This is the same encryption standard used by banks and governments.
security.encryptionTodayBody2: Each user has a unique encryption key derived from a master secret using HKDF (HMAC-based Key Derivation Function). This means that even if the database were compromised, encrypted fields cannot be decrypted without the application-layer keys.
security.encryptionTodayBody3: Emails are additionally hashed with SHA-256 + a secret pepper for lookups, so the plaintext email is never used as a database key.
security.whatGetsEncrypted2: Encounter journal notes and custom field values
security.transportBody: All communication between your device and Navilla is encrypted in transit using HTTPS/TLS. We enforce secure transport across all environments.
security.authBody: Authentication uses token-based session management via Supabase Auth. Passwords are never stored in plain text. Sessions expire and require re-authentication. Refresh tokens are rotated on every use.
security.accessBody: The backend API validates every request against your session token before returning any data. You can only access data that belongs to you. No data is publicly accessible without authentication.
security.roadmapBody1: Our current architecture encrypts data at the application layer — the server encrypts and decrypts on your behalf. This protects against database breaches and unauthorized access, but it means the server can technically read your data during processing.
security.roadmapBody2: We are working toward true end-to-end encryption (E2EE), where your data is encrypted on your device before it ever leaves, and only your device holds the keys. This is the model used by Signal and Telegram's secret chats — the server becomes a blind relay that stores data it cannot read.
security.roadmapBody3: The goal: even if Navilla's servers were fully compromised, your health data, partner names, and encounter history would remain unreadable.
security.e2eePlan1: Client-side key generation — encryption keys created and stored on your device
security.e2eePlan2: Zero-knowledge storage — the server stores only ciphertext it cannot decrypt
security.e2eePlan3: Secure key backup — optional encrypted key backup for device recovery, protected by a passphrase only you know
security.e2eePlan4: Multi-device sync — secure key transfer between your devices using established protocols
security.whatWeDoNotDo1: We do not use third-party tracking scripts or analytics SDKs
security.whatWeDoNotDo2: We do not embed advertising networks
security.whatWeDoNotDo3: We do not share your data with data brokers
security.whatWeDoNotDo4: We do not store health data in unencrypted form
security.emailSecurityBody: Transactional email is configured with modern domain authentication controls (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) to reduce spoofing risk.
security.vulnerabilityBody: If you discover a security vulnerability in Navilla, please report it responsibly to contact@navilla.app. We take all reports seriously and will respond promptly.
